title: Prediction market odds on Tesla-SpaceX merger are above 50% for early 2027
source_used: New York Post (which relays Bloomberg's report on Barclays)
key_facts: Kalshi bettors put the odds of a Tesla and SpaceX merger at over 50% for early next year (2027).
On Kalshi's question 'When will Tesla and SpaceX merge?': about 50% by 1 March, nearly 60% by 1 April and nearly 80% by the end of next year; low odds for the rest of this year.
Barclays analysts, quoted by Bloomberg, said a merger could happen before Tesla's annual general meeting, due by 6 December, and that it has increasingly become the consensus expectation.
Barclays noted challenges including winning shareholder votes; about 11% of votes at Tesla's 2025 meeting were broker non-votes, counted effectively as against.
SpaceX, valued at nearly $2 trillion, went public in June; Tesla is worth roughly $1.4 trillion; SpaceX earlier merged with Musk's AI business xAI.
Musk unveiled a new Tesla Roadster, described as 'flying', with SpaceX technology at a SpaceX test site in Texas on Thursday 15 Oct 2026.
SpaceX and Tesla did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
quote_evidence: Elon Musk's unveiling of a new "flying" Tesla on a SpaceX site this week has observers buzzing about an out-of-this-world merger between the two companies, with Kalshi bettors putting the odds of such a combo at over 50% for early next year.
"The possibility of a Tesla/SpaceX merger has increasingly become the consensus expectation," Barclays analysts wrote this week, according to Bloomberg.
SpaceX and Tesla did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: A possible merger of two companies worth over $3 trillion combined would affect shareholders of both.
event_date: 15-16 Oct 2026 (Roadster unveiled 15 Oct; odds reported 16 Oct)
notes: CNBC original (pool item) blocked (Akamai error page). Its headline matches ('above 50% for early 2027'). Used the New York Post, which reports the Kalshi odds itself and relays Bloomberg on Barclays. Odds are a betting market's view, not evidence of a plan.
